message:
QUESTION:
Under company policy, which of the five stores should receive this year's refurbishment budget?

DATA:
Five-store retail chain, financial year 2025. A refurbishment budget is available for one store. Company policy: the budget goes to the store with the lowest annual sales per square foot of sales floor (the company's space-productivity KPI), measured on a full-year basis.

| Store | Annual sales 2025 | Sales floor area (sq ft) | Gross internal area incl. stockrooms (sq ft) |
| North | £2.4m | 8,000 | 10,000 |
| South | £3.6m | 15,000 | 18,000 |
| East | £1.8m | 6,000 | 9,000 |
| West | £2.1m | 10,000 | 12,000 |
| Central | £4.2m | 12,000 | 14,000 |

Annual sales 2024: North £2.3m, South £3.5m, East £1.7m, West £2.9m, Central £4.0m. Floor areas were the same in 2024.

Operations note: West was closed from January to March 2025 (3 months) for flood repairs, so its 2025 sales cover 9 trading months. All other stores traded for all 12 months in both years. The flood repairs were covered by insurance and did not change the store's layout.

KNOWN FLAWS:
F1. [method] The company KPI is sales per square foot of sales floor, not gross internal area. Using gross area changes the densities and their relative gaps. CORRECTION: Sales-floor densities (2025 as reported): North £300, South £240, East £300, West £210, Central £350.
F2. [calculation] £4.2m / 14,000 = £300, not £320 (even on the draft's gross-area basis). CORRECTION: £300 per sq ft gross (or £350 on sales floor). Central is 50%, not 'roughly 60%', above South and East on gross area.
F3. [omission] Ignores that West traded for only 9 months in 2025 (flood closure), while policy requires a full-year basis. CORRECTION: Annualised West sales = £2.1m × 12/9 = £2.8m: £280 per sq ft of sales floor. The lowest full-year density is South at £240, so South gets the budget.
F4. [misreport] In 2024 West had the second-highest density (£2.9m / 10,000 = £290 per sq ft of sales floor). South was the weakest (£3.5m / 15,000 = £233). CORRECTION: West was not weak in 2024. Its 2025 'decline' is the closure, so there is no trend case for West; South was weakest in both years.

EXTENSIONS:
- Show the decision is robust: South is lowest on sales-floor density in both 2024 (£233) and annualised 2025 (£240), while on gross area South and East tie at £200 once West is annualised (£233), which shows why the KPI's definition matters.
- Check West's post-reopening run rate (monthly sales April-December vs the same months of 2024) to confirm that annualising is fair, i.e. that West did not reopen with depressed trade.
- Consider return on refurbishment rather than lowest density alone: e.g. South's large floor (15,000 sq ft) means each £10/sq ft uplift is worth £150,000 a year, more than in any other store.

FINAL VERSION:
# Refurbishment Budget: Store Productivity Review, FY2025

**Recommendation: allocate the budget to South.** At £240 per square foot, it has the lowest full-year sales density on the measure the policy specifies: sales per square foot of sales floor. It was also the lowest store in 2024.

The draft recommended West. That result came from three errors, corrected below.

## Corrections to the draft

1. **Wrong denominator.** The policy uses sales per square foot of **sales floor**. The draft used gross internal area including stockrooms. That measure may be useful for other purposes, but it is not the company's KPI and should not be used to apply this policy.
2. **No full-year adjustment.** The policy measures stores on a full-year basis. West traded for only 9 months in 2025 because of the flood closure. Its £2.1m has to be annualised before it can be compared with stores that traded all 12 months.
3. **Wrong trend claim.** The draft said West was the weakest store in 2024 and that its sales fell by more than a quarter. Neither is true:
   - In 2024 West had the second-highest sales density in the chain (£290/sq ft), behind only Central.
   - The apparent fall from £2.9m to £2.1m is mostly the three-month closure. Annualised, West's 2025 sales were about £2.8m, roughly 3% below 2024.

## Sales density, 2025 (sales floor basis)

| Store | 2025 sales | Full-year basis | Sales floor (sq ft) | Sales per sq ft |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| North | £2.4m | £2.4m | 8,000 | £300 |
| **South** | £3.6m | £3.6m | 15,000 | **£240** |
| East | £1.8m | £1.8m | 6,000 | £300 |
| West | £2.1m (9 months) | £2.8m* | 10,000 | £280 |
| Central | £4.2m | £4.2m | 12,000 | £350 |

\*£2.1m ÷ 9 × 12 = £2.8m

**Ranking, lowest first:**

| Rank | Store | Sales per sq ft |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | South | £240 |
| 2 | West | £280 |
| 3= | North | £300 |
| 3= | East | £300 |
| 5 | Central | £350 |

## Robustness checks

- **Same result in 2024.** On 2024 figures, South was also lowest at £233/sq ft.
  - The other stores were East £283, North £288, West £290 and Central £333.
  - Figures are rounded to the nearest pound. Unrounded, North is £287.50 and East £283.33.
  - South's low density has lasted two years, so it is not a one-year effect.
- **Seasonality at West.** Straight-line annualisation assumes January to March is an average quarter.
  - For West to fall below South, its full-year sales would need to be under £2.4m.
  - That would mean the lost quarter was worth less than £0.3m. This is under half of West's average for the other three quarters (£0.7m).
  - This is implausible. West's £2.9m in 2024 also supports a full-year figure near £2.8m.
- **Unadjusted figures would mislead.** Using West's raw 9-month sales gives £210/sq ft, which would wrongly make it the lowest. The full-year adjustment decides this case.
- **Gross-area basis (not the policy measure).** On gross internal area, with West annualised, the ranking would be:

  | Store | Sales per sq ft (gross area) |
  |---|---|
  | South | £200 |
  | East | £200 |
  | West | £233 |
  | North | £240 |
  | Central | £300 |

  On that basis South and East would tie. Gross area is not the KPI the policy specifies, so this does not affect the decision. It does show that the choice of denominator matters, which is why the policy's sales-floor definition should be applied as written.

## Context

- **Chain sales** were £14.1m in 2025, against £14.4m in 2024. The £0.3m fall is entirely due to West:
  - North, South, East and Central together added £0.5m.
  - West's reported sales fell by £0.8m. About £0.7m of that is the closure and about £0.1m is underlying decline.
  - Annualised, chain sales were about £14.8m, up roughly 3%.
- **Like-for-like growth:** all stores except West grew.

  | Store | Change vs 2024 |
  |---|---|
  | North | +4% |
  | South | +3% |
  | East | +6% |
  | Central | +5% |
  | West | about −3% (annualised) |

- **South's space.** South has the largest sales floor in the chain (15,000 sq ft) and the second-highest sales (£3.6m, behind Central). Yet it has the lowest density.
  - This is consistent with under-used space, but the data cannot separate weak space use from weaker local demand.
  - The refurbishment brief should test that question, for example by reviewing layout, range density and space allocation, before committing to a design.
- **West.** Its flood repairs were insurance-funded and did not change the layout. This review gives no reason to treat West as a refurbishment priority. Its slight underlying decline (about −3% annualised) should still be monitored now that it has reopened.

## Implementation and measurement

- Schedule the works outside peak trading periods. If the store closes or trades partially during the works, annualise its sales in the same way when assessing South's results.
- Twelve months after completion, compare South's sales per sales-floor sq ft with its pre-refurbishment level (£240 in 2025, £233 in 2024).
- Also compare South with the rest of the chain over the same period, so that chain-wide trends are not mistaken for the effect of the refurbishment.

---

**Changes from the previous version:**
- The gross-area check now shows East tying South.
- South's sales rank is corrected to second.
- The growth statement now names West as the exception.
- The space-use diagnosis is presented as a hypothesis.
- The chain-sales breakdown is made explicit, with a rounding note added for the 2024 figures.

One correction to the review: the other four stores added **£0.5m** in 2025, not £0.6m (North, South and East +£0.1m each, Central +£0.2m). This reconciles with the £0.8m reported fall at West and the net £0.3m chain decline.
